payload.source_label: In a one-step method the solution at the next time level is determined entirely by data at the current time level

contract.statement: Section 1.7 explains that the book primarily considers one-step numerical methods: the numerical solution at t_{n+1} is determined entirely by data at t_n. This explains why temporal superscripts are often suppressed; Q and other numerical quantities without such a superscript generally refer to the current time level. The passage does not specify the contents of that data or an update formula (raw PDF page 32, printed page 10, Section 1.7, second paragraph, anchors: 'one-step methods', 'data at time t_n', and 'current time level t_n is intended').
assumptions: The dependence claim concerns a one-step numerical method of the kind primarily considered in the book (raw PDF page 32, printed page 10, Section 1.7, second paragraph, anchor: 'we primarily consider one-step methods').

The selected claim is explanatory prose in a notation section, rather than a numbered theorem or a specified update formula (raw PDF page 32, printed page 10, heading '1.7 Notation' and second paragraph).

Interpreting 'solution' in the one-step sentence as the numerical solution is supported by the enclosing paragraph's introduction of Q and its subsequent reference to 'other numerical quantities' (raw PDF page 32, printed page 10, Section 1.7, second paragraph).
quantifiers: n identifies the current time level t_n, and n+1 identifies the next time level t_{n+1}; the paragraph does not explicitly specify an index set or write a universal quantifier (raw PDF page 32, printed page 10, Section 1.7, second paragraph, anchor: 'superscript n denotes time level t_n').
i, or i and j in two dimensions, are spatial indices in Q_i^n and Q_ij^n (raw PDF page 32, printed page 10, Section 1.7, second paragraph, anchor: 'Subscripts on Q denote spatial locations').
